newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 30.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest-July 30.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

BERLIN - In the face of sinking alcohol consumption in Germany, the advertising and beverage industries step up their campaign to defeat proposed restrictions on advertising for beer, wine and liquor. "There is no reason to further limit freedom of speech and freedom to conduct business, which are basic rights in a free market," Germany's central advertising group (ZAW) and alcohol industry representatives say in a joint statement. (Reuter)

DUESSELDORF - The New York headquarters of advertising group Euro RSCG has approved funds for wider investment, paving the way for worldwide expansion, German unit chief executive Gerhard Schoeps says. "This investment (also) creates the foundation for greater development in Germany," Schoeps says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Ingo Krauss, chairman and chief executive officer of advertising group Young & Rubicam's German unit, is leaving the agency after almost 30 years, industry magazine Text Intern says. Krauss will be replaced by the former chief executive of the group's Dutch unit, Tiemen Bosma, Text Intern says. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Henninger brewers is going through a consolidation phase in which its entire marketing strategy is being re-evaluated, marketing director Paul Ritter says. Current advertising account holder Bates will keep the account until the end of the year and at a minimum manage some projects next year, Ritter says. But Euro RSCG in Duesseldorf has already taken charge of some campaigns. (Horizont)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - Daimler-Benz AG is likely to show net profit more than doubled in the first half of this year when the industrial conglomorate holds its annual mid-year press conference in London on Thursday. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Volkswagen and Audi AG, its luxury carmaker unit, have announced special shifts during August and through the rest of the year in a bid to reduce delivery times for popular models. (Reuter)

BERLIN - Dresdner Bank AG says it will fill its war chest for a possible purchase in the U.S. and forge closer ties with insurer Allianz AG to reinforce its position in a sector hellbent on consolidation. (Reuter)

HERZOGENAURACH - Adidas AG says it will stay in Germany and build a new headquarters on a former American military base close to the Bavarian town where Adi Dassler founded the sportswear group in 1920. (Reuter)

MUNICH - Computer distributor Computer 2000 AG says strong market growth in Europe spurred a 23.4 percent rise in group sales in the first nine months of 1996/97 to 6.28 billion marks ($3.4 billion). (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Mannesmann AG says it plans to apply for a license to provide mobile phone service in Luxembourg through a venture called Luxcall. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
FRANKFURT - Knut Rittberger starts in the new position of marketing and sales director for Europe at Sixt auto rental KG in Munich. (Horizont)
